svg.title: ArdaRenderGraph end-to-end example diagrams
svg.desc: Eight diagrams covering culling, swap-chain presentation, async compute, copy queues, transient reuse, extraction across frames, triangle upload, and per-frame triangle rendering.

g.title: Minimal produce, consume, and cull graph
g.desc: The live path runs from GraphPrologue through Produce and Consume to GraphEpilogue. A Dead pass writes DeadOutput but reaches no observable root and is culled.
g.text: Produce, consume, and cull dead work
Extraction makes Output observable; the compiler retains only its backward dependency chain.

g.title: Swap-chain frame and acquire-present loop
g.desc: The application acquires a presentable framebuffer, imports its color texture, executes a raster pass, transitions it back to Present in the epilogue, prepares submission, executes, presents, and begins another frame.
g.text: External swap-chain image: acquire, render, submit, present
The application owns acquire and present; the graph owns declared resource transitions and submission.

g.title: Async compute fork and graphics join
g.desc: ProduceInput runs on graphics, AsyncFilter runs on compute, and Composite returns to graphics. Cross-queue resource edges insert waits at the fork and join. If compute is unavailable, all work falls back to graphics.
g.text: Async compute fork and graphics join
Resource dependencies crossing queue domains become explicit queue waits.
No compute queue: AsyncFilter falls back to Graphics and these cross-queue waits disappear.

g.title: Copy queue import, copy, and extraction
g.desc: A physical source buffer is imported as CopySource. A copy pass writes a graph-created destination as CopyDest on the copy queue when available. The epilogue transitions and extracts the result as CopySource.
g.text: Copy queue: import, copy, and extract
The Copy pass falls back to Graphics when no dedicated copy queue exists.
graph-created destination becomes the returned physical handle

g.title: Transient A and B reuse timeline
g.desc: Transient A is live at execution index one and Transient B is live at index two. Because their compatible intervals do not overlap in one queue domain, both can use the same committed pooled allocation.
g.text: Descriptor-compatible transient resources reuse one allocation
This is committed-resource pooling, not placed-resource aliasing.
A releases before B acquires the descriptor-compatible resource

g.title: Extraction across frames
g.desc: Frame N builds history as an unordered access texture, transitions it to ShaderResource in the epilogue, and returns the extracted NVRHI handle. After application-managed frame synchronization, Frame N plus one imports that handle in ShaderResource and reads it.
g.text: Extract history in Frame N, then import it in Frame N+1
Extraction returns a handle after submission; GPU completion remains application-managed.

g.title: Triangle upload graph
g.desc: External vertex and index buffers enter in their rendering states. One graphics-queue pass transitions both to CopyDest and writes their data. The epilogue restores VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer, then the application waits for idle.
g.text: The pass uses flags None, records on Graphics, and issues two real writeBuffer commands.

g.title: Per-frame triangle render graph
g.desc: The application acquires a framebuffer. The graph imports its presentable color texture and persistent vertex and index buffers. A raster pass clears and draws, the epilogue restores Present, then the application prepares submission, executes the graph, and presents.
g.text: One Raster pass consumes persistent geometry and writes the acquired color attachment.
